source:
Maya: The city's study says the new interchange will cut cut-through traffic by a third. I am convinced.
Deshawn: The study was commissioned by the same developer who owns the land next to the interchange. I do not take their modeling at face value.
Maya: The methodology chapter is solid. Independent reviewers signed off on the model.
Deshawn: Reviewers chosen and paid by the department that wants the project built. If an environmental group had funded the same model, you would question it too.
Maya: That is not fair. I would evaluate the methods either way.
Deshawn: Maybe, but my point stands: until someone unaffiliated reruns the model, the a-third figure is marketing.

extraction.mainQuestion: Can the city's interchange study be trusted as the basis for a decision?

positions.label: Accept the study
positions.thesis: The city's interchange study is trustworthy because its methodology was independently reviewed.
positions.steelman: Evaluating methods on their merits, with signed-off review, is exactly how good analysis should be accepted regardless of who paid.

groundingQuotes.quote: The city's study says the new interchange will cut cut-through traffic by a third.
Independent reviewers signed off on the model.

positions.label: Withhold trust until replication
positions.thesis: The study's figures should not be trusted until an unaffiliated party reruns the model, given who commissioned and reviewed it.
positions.steelman: Funding and reviewer selection shape conclusions in practice, so interested-party research warrants independent replication before it drives decisions.

groundingQuotes.quote: until someone unaffiliated reruns the model, the a-third figure is marketing.

claims.statement: The study's traffic model was reviewed by independent methodologists and is sound.

resolution.condition: Disclose the reviewers' selection process and conflicts so independence can be assessed.

groundingQuotes.quote: Independent reviewers signed off on the model.

claims.statement: A study commissioned by a party with a financial stake, and reviewed by a department that wants the project, should not be trusted without independent replication.

resolution.condition: An unaffiliated team reruns the model and publishes inputs and code.

groundingQuotes.quote: The study was commissioned by the same developer who owns the land next to the interchange.

commonGroundCandidates.statement: Both participants are talking about the same forecast figure of roughly one-third less cut-through traffic.

groundingQuotes.quote: cut cut-through traffic by a third

disagreementCandidates.question: Should the city's interchange study be trusted given who commissioned and reviewed it?
disagreementCandidates.summary: The object-level dispute is really about whether the study's funding and review chain disqualify it.

participantStances.stance: Yes; the methods were independently signed off.
No; interested funders and hand-picked reviewers require replication.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Independent rerun of the model by an unaffiliated team.

disagreementCandidates.question: Would Maya evaluate identical methods differently if the funder's interests were reversed?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Deshawn asserts a funding double standard; Maya denies evaluating methods differently.

participantStances.stance: I would evaluate the methods either way.
You would question the same model from an environmental group.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Some test of stated standards against revealed practice across funders.

caveats: This maps a source-trust dispute; it does not audit the actual study or its reviewers.
